I've watched the decline in quality of content and comments in Digg, Reddit, and many other aggregators over ~10 years. I now arrive at Voat and want to share my thoughts on how the Eternal September problem could be handled on this site.

Alpha users will shape the initial quality of content/comments on this site. Let's assume Alpha users are drawn to this site because it's meant to be uncensored, informative, and insightful. As newer users arrive at Voat it is likely that many of them will be attracted to its popularity and as an alternative to Reddit rather than the initial purpose that drew the Alpha user base in. The new users will likely submit comments and content that reflects that attraction and that will become more problematic over time.

In order to preserve the initial user base's quality of content/comments a different way of sorting could be implemented. Voating remains the same; however, the ability to sort content/comments by user class/user account age is added. Alpha, Beta, 1 year, 2 years, etc. Perhaps content by older users would be made slightly more visible as time passes (maybe a different font color/type). Granted, this could create a lot of users with too much visibility/influence, but perhaps that could be mitigated in some way (all voats for content/comments by former Alpha users count as a 1/2 voat?).

I don't expect this submission to lead to anything and I haven't the slightest idea about implementation/feasibility. Someone has probably already thought of something similar/better, but I figured it might be worth a shot.
Digg > Reddit > Voat --- Preservation of Initial Quality of Content/Comments

The inherent issue with this idea is that this goes against one of the reasons why users might have left Reddit for Voat. Most users wouldn't want to be controlled by a person who has an elevated status. This is partially the problem with moderators being able to censor content submitted by other users. Censorship is a form of power that not ever user has access to on Reddit, and for good reason; but some might take this idea that Alpha or Beta users would be able to push other content aside if it was submitted by a 1 year or 2 year account. Which I find isn't fair.

It's on the userbase to submit quality content, and if a tipping point does come where quantity overcomes quality, than Voat did not succeed in attracting the right userbase.

To add to this, it's also up to the userbase to vote appropriately. For example, we might all agree that memes are stupid, but banning them outright it against the spirit of the site. Instead, the users should vote correctly, actively discouraging the submission of that type of content. If the majority of the userbase exposed to the bad content votes correctly, then it won't matter if a bunch of teenagers are brigading said content, because they won't be able to overcome the entire userbase. And if the teentards become the majority (like what happened to Digg), then it's time for another site.

The problem with the above is that the people submitting the shit content want to do it on sites that are popular and "cool". They too want to avoid an echo chamber! However, we have no method of preventing the people who would submit that crap from joining and doing just that. We just have to nuke it when it gets here.
